input.quote: shall continue in operation for at least an initial period of twenty-five (25) years following the RFS Date (hereinafter referred to as "initial Period") and shall be terminable thereafter by agreement of the Parties. However, any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter by giving not less than one (1) year's prior notice thereof, in writing, to the other Parties.
input.rationale: Paragraph 18 is the only exit mechanic. Para 18.1 commits every Party, including us, for a 25-year Initial Period and permits unilateral withdrawal only at or after the end of that period on one year's notice; para 18.2 allows mid-term termination only by unanimous written agreement or a 90% Management Committee majority. There is therefore no Customer convenience exit in a multi-year term, which is expressly walk-away territory and fails the fallback on Customer notice. Paragraph 23 (default/capacity reclamation) is a for-cause mechanic and supplies no convenience right. The counterparty side is already acceptable: no other Party may unilaterally withdraw during the Initial Period and end-of-term withdrawal requires a full year's notice, so the "no Vendor convenience right during a committed term" element is already met and is not re-drafted. We add one numbered Subparagraph 18.1A carrying only the still-missing elements, phrased so that the Customer's right to terminate for convenience is stated on the face of the clause: the Customer may terminate this Agreement or its participation for convenience, on not more than 30 days' prior written notice, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts. Residual note only: the retained sentence "No credit for capital costs will be made to a Party that terminates its participation in accordance with Subparagraph 18.1" is keyed to 18.1 alone and so cannot attach to a withdrawal under 18.1A; that money term is held for the liquidated-damages rule to avoid double-flagging.

proposal.summary: Insert numbered Subparagraph 18.1A: the Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Paragraph 18.1 locks us in for a 25-year Initial Period with no convenience exit, which is our walk-away position. We have added a numbered Subparagraph 18.1A under which we, as Customer, may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts; the other Parties' exit right remains limited to the end of the Initial Period on one year's notice. If you prefer, we can move to our fallback of 60-90 days' notice with any early-termination fee capped at three months' charges.

ops.text: 18.1A Notwithstanding Subparagraph 18.1, Teleglobe USA Inc. is referred to in this Subparagraph 18.1A as the "Customer", and the Customer may terminate this Agreement or its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time, including during the Initial Period, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Parties, and the other Parties shall refund to the Customer, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by it in respect of the period after the effective date of such termination.
